newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces renewal of MFN for China.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces renewal of MFN for China.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton announced on Monday the renewal of China's most favored nation trade privileges for another year.
The decision was expected to set off a fierce debate in the U.S. Congress, which has the right to overturn Clinton's decision.

"I have decided, as all my predecessors have since 1980, to extend most favoured nation status to China for the coming year," Clinton told businessmen in a White House speech. "I believe if we were to revoke normal trade status it would cut off our contact with the Chinese people and undermine our influence with the Chinese government."

Clinton noted that the United States had differences with China, particularly over human rights, but said he believed MFN status should still be maintained. "Our broad policy is engagement. That doesn't mean that we win every point, but it means we work together when we can and we're honest in our disagreements when they exist," he added.
Clinton must inform Congress by June 3 of his decision to extend MFN, which is normal trade status for all but a handful of nations including Cuba, Vietnam and North Korea.

To reverse his decision, the House and Senate must pass a joint resolution disapproving it by Aug. 31. If Clinton were to veto the move, both chambers then would have to muster a two-thirds majority to override his veto.
